item.title: Police Report Details Gun Threat: Doherty’s girlfriend alleges armed breakup fight; case yet to reach court
item.description: Jack Doherty’s girlfriend allegedly pulled a firearm during an argument over their breakup before his September arrest, according to a Fort Lauderdale police report obtained by TMZ. She told officers she feared Doherty and had warned she would shoot him if he came closer. Doherty denied touching her and showed officers security footage that he said supported his account.

item.title: 'Tarique hasn't ruled out India visit': Dhaka
item.description: Bangladesh has highlighted the importance of trust and bilateral engagement for future relations with India. State Minister Humaiun Kobir stated that preventing extremists in India from making destabilizing statements is necessary. He mentioned that mutual respect is required for maintaining good relations between the two countries. A potential visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India is under consideration, emphasizing direct dialogue.
item.dc:creator: Ahsan Tasnim

item.title: Nepal ends flood search with over 5,000 still missing, including 189 Indians
item.description: Nepal has suspended non-essential search operations after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods that occurred on August 26. The floods resulted in 1,455 deaths, with 5,285 people still unaccounted for, including many foreign tourists. Among the missing individuals are 189 Indians, along with tourists from various other countries. The government has shifted its focus towards reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts rather than continuing search operations.
item.dc:creator: Vishant Agarwala

item.title: Couple turns 2 garden plots into 50-acre farm; 2.5 acres hit $200K in sales
item.description: Shane and Emma Rozeveld's journey from hobby gardeners in British Columbia to running a thriving 50-acre organic farm in Ontario is inspiring. Founders of Aslan Organics since 2017, they navigated challenges at the Sarnia Farmers' Market, eventually boosting their revenue to over $200,000 in a single year with weekly sales hitting $10,000.

item.title: Pakistan, Saudi, Turkiye activate Mecca defence pact as Yemen war escalates
item.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to enhance military cooperation to address regional security threats. Following recent attacks by Yemen's Houthi group, the three countries will activate collective deterrence measures. The emergency meeting of the Mecca Defence Alliance in Riyadh led to this commitment. Saudi-backed forces are also launching an offensive against the Houthis in Yemen to regain control.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Not now daal-ing, says MAGA, as Montana governor comes to India to sell pulses
item.description: Montana's Governor Greg Gianforte is heading a delegation to India to promote agricultural exports. The focus is on selling lentils, peas, and chickpeas to the world's largest consumer of pulses. This trip highlights the growing tension within the Republican party regarding international trade and immigration. Many in the GOP criticize Gianforte's outreach to India amidst concerns about jobs for Americans.

item.title: Elvis Presley raised $65,000 for USS Arizona Memorial; crewmen remain entombed in Pearl Harbor wreck
item.description: Elvis Presley raised $65,000 towards the USS Arizona Memorial in 1961. Completed that year and dedicated in 1962, the 184-foot memorial spans the sunken battleship at Pearl Harbor, where more than 900 crewmen remain entombed.

item.title: D’Arros shearwater colony grew nearly 10-fold after rats were eradicated
item.description: D'Arros Island's Wedge-tailed Shearwater population rose dramatically after rats were eradicated in 2003. Researchers recorded 2,768 breeding pairs in 2016 and 2,406 pairs in 2021. The colony spread across a larger area and exhibited higher breeding burrow density during later surveys. The study utilized direct counts and area-based estimates to determine breeding pair numbers. Identifying the peak incubation period in November was crucial for future population comparisons.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: California family’s 6,625-acre ranch is now protected forever
item.description: The Kinsey family has strategically safeguarded their vast 6,625-acre ranch in Benbow, California, by implementing a conservation easement. This crucial step preserves the land's agricultural, forest, and wildlife values, ensuring the ranch's ongoing functionality while protecting vital habitats for endangered species. David Johnson, a family member, was instrumental in this initiative, with the Northcoast Regional Land Trust planning to acknowledge their dedication to conservation this coming October.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After losing her mother to MS, J.K. Rowling gave £10m to research
item.description: J.K. Rowling opened the Anne Rowling Regenerative Neurology Clinic in memory of her mother, who died of multiple sclerosis. The clinic focuses on research and treatment of various neurological diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease. The funding aims to attract world-class researchers to develop new therapies and potentially find a cure. It has already hosted numerous clinical appointments and research projects since its inception.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Man pays $15, finds 6.03-carat diamond worth $1M
item.description: Jack Pearadin, a dedicated Navy reservist from Missouri, has transformed his passion into a treasure hunt since 2013 at Arkansas's Crater of Diamonds State Park. Recently, his persistence paid off when he discovered a stunning 6.03-carat yellow diamond he estimates could be worth $1 million. Throughout his adventurous quest, Pearadin has unearthed over 300 gems, sharing the profits from his latest find, aptly named the 'American Dream,' with a friend.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dad built a backyard coaster, now selling it for NZ$4,500
item.description: In the midst of the COVID-19 lockdown, inspired by a flurry of YouTube tutorials, Bjorn Burton took on an exciting challenge—he built a roller coaster in his backyard. With his father’s help, he engineered this thrilling ride after rigorous safety trials with concrete bags. Now that the neighborhood kids have outgrown it, Bjorn is ready to sell the coaster, already envisioning a future project for when he welcomes grandchildren.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: American chestnut returns to Bronx Zoo after 120 years; 25 saplings planted in NYC
item.description: The American chestnut is returning to the Bronx Zoo more than 120 years after blight was first documented there. The zoo and New York Restoration Project planted 25 hybrid saplings as part of a restoration effort. Once abundant across eastern North America, the tree was devastated by disease that killed nearly 4 billion trees.
